transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
Hi, thank you for seeing me. When I'm alone working late, I start eating and it feels like I can't stop or control how much I'm eating until it's over. It's just really starting to worry me.

Do these episodes of eating large amounts happen only when you are alone and working late, or do they also happen in other situations? Also, do you ever try to make up for them by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising?

They mostly happen when I'm alone, and I'll actually wait until my roommate goes to bed so I can eat in my room without her seeing, sometimes even after I've already had a normal dinner. I don't ever try to throw up, use laxatives, or over-exercise to make up for it; I just feel incredibly sluggish and ashamed the next day.
About how often do these episodes happen, for example how many times per week or month? And have they been going on for at least 3 months?

These episodes have been happening at least once a week, and sometimes more often when I have big work deadlines. This whole pattern has been going on for about ten months now, starting shortly after I got promoted to senior designer.
When these episodes happen, do you eat a clearly large amount of food in a short time, or is it more that you feel out of control while eating a normal amount?

It is definitely a very large amount of food eaten in a short window of time. I'll often order enough takeout for three people—like two entrees, sides, and dessert—and eat it all along with snacks within an hour or two. Once I start, a switch just flips and I feel completely out of control, like I can't stop myself.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about your weight or body shape, or ever try to restrict food, fast, or exercise because of how you feel about your body?

No, I don't really focus on my weight or try to restrict food or exercise to compensate. These episodes are much more driven by my work stress and feeling completely out of control, rather than concerns about my body image.
Do you ever have periods between these episodes when you purposely eat very little or skip meals because you are afraid of losing control again?

No, I don't purposely restrict my food or skip meals out of fear of losing control. Any skipped meals are usually just because I'm so busy with work and lose track of time, rather than an attempt to prevent another episode.
During these eating episodes, do you feel a strong sense of distress, guilt, or shame while they are happening or right afterward?

Yes, I feel an overwhelming amount of shame and distress, especially right after it happens. I'm so embarrassed that I hide my eating from my roommate, and the next day the guilt is so bad that I end up canceling plans and just hiding in my apartment.
Have you ever had a significant fear of gaining weight or strong concerns about your body shape or size, even if you do not act on them?

No, I haven't really had a significant fear of gaining weight or any major concerns about my body shape. The real distress for me is just the feeling of completely losing control in the moment and the heavy shame that comes right after.

Have you ever had episodes of eating a large amount of food followed by trying to make up for it by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising, or by being very worried about your weight or body shape?

No, I have never done anything like vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising to make up for what I ate. I also don't really worry about my weight or body shape. For me, the real issue is just that terrifying feeling of losing complete control in the moment.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unable to control eating but it was not clearly a large amount of food, or where the episodes did not meet all of the binge-eating features I asked about?
No, I haven't really experienced that. My episodes almost always involve eating a clearly massive amount of food, and I don't recall any times where I lost control over just a small or normal amount.
